subject: AAE-R1B R3(iii)/R4: fourteen new Explore lessons from the canonical register. The original AAE section5 is not present; the medium choices and week distribution here are conservative implementation choices, not a quotation of that unseen clause.

level.title: Entry Level Award in the Arts
level.unitStructure: four parts, each a DISTINCT activity

A.name: Take part
A.requires: at least two arts activities; identify what they learnt

B.name: Explore
B.requires: at least one artist AND at least one arts ORGANISATION, through live or active experience
B.note: Desk research alone fails. "Active participation" means beyond desk research only.

C.name: Create
C.requires: an artwork, a record of the PROCESS, and the final work

D.name: Share
D.requires: communicate personal enjoyment or achievement, chosen by looking back at A-C

level.attemptedRule: Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass.

rows.title: Try Drawing With Line
rows.outcome: Take part in drawing: learn and try controlled line choices. Record what was actually done and an initial learning point. This begins activity one.

rows.title: Use Tone And Say What I Learnt
rows.outcome: Continue the drawing activity with taught tone techniques. Preserve a selected result and the pupil’s account of learning. Identify this as the same activity, not a second one.

rows.title: Build With Folded Paper
rows.outcome: Take part in a distinct paper-sculpture activity: learn safe folds and ways to make paper stand. Keep a record of participation. This is activity two.

rows.title: Test A Join And Compare My Learning
rows.outcome: Continue paper sculpture with taught joining/stability techniques. Identify what was learnt in both arts activities, using the pupil’s actual work and words. Do not require numerical improvement for Explore.

rows.title: Get Ready To Explore An Artist And Organisation
rows.outcome: Prepare questions and distinguish an artist’s work from an organisation’s role. Read PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT; keep research/rehearsal labelled preparation. This deck alone does not complete Part B.

rows.title: Explore An Artist Through A Live Activity
rows.outcome: Undertake first-hand live/active exploration through the actual route. Record the real artist, activity, what the pupil explored and the evidence location after it happened.

rows.title: Explore What An Arts Organisation Does
rows.outcome: Undertake live/active exploration of the actual organisation and its arts work. Record the organisation’s identity, what the pupil actively explored and its source/experience record. Reading a website alone is preparation.

rows.title: Connect The Artist, Organisation And What I Found
rows.outcome: Work from actual experience records. Explain or demonstrate what was found about the artist and the organisation and how their roles connect. Check that both are evidenced. Complete a missing live/active element when arranged; do not fill it with an invented account.

rows.title: Choose A New Artwork To Make
rows.outcome: Begin a distinct creation activity. Make the pupil’s own choice of an artwork and accessible tools, informed by previous learning without reusing a finished A/B activity as C. Preserve the starting idea as process evidence.

rows.title: Start Making And Keep The Process
rows.outcome: Teach the needed next technique and begin the chosen artwork. Preserve actual stages through work samples, credited photographs, short notes, or located recordings.

rows.title: Develop The Work And Record A Choice
rows.outcome: Continue making. Teach a useful material/process decision and record what the pupil chose and did. Preserve earlier states before changing them; a ring on overwritten work is not a before-state record.

rows.title: Finish The Artwork And Show Its Making
rows.outcome: Complete the artwork and assemble a trace of its real process. Evidence must contain both process and final work, not only a final image or only a plan.

rows.title: Look Back And Choose What To Share
rows.outcome: Look across A–C; pupil chooses personal enjoyment or achievement to communicate, and an accessible format. Prepare/rehearse this distinct sharing activity using the pupil’s own words and choices.

rows.title: Share My Enjoyment Or Achievement
rows.outcome: Actually communicate the chosen enjoyment or achievement. Keep an accurate record of what was communicated and how, with a locator. Check all four part records without presenting a folder audit alone as Part D.
